primitives.name: Sign-Gestalt Expectation
primitives.verbatim_quote: Stimuli corresponding to all parts of the signgestalt, i.e., sign, significate and signified means-end relations, are present.
primitives.assumptions: The organism perceives the complete signgestalt including the sign, significate, and the full means-end relation structure.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Perception occurs when all stimulus components are simultaneously present; absence of any component leads to alternative cognitive processes.

layer2.mapping: Maps the signgestalt to a joint probability distribution over sign, significate, and means-end relations, P(sign, significate, means-end). Perception corresponds to non-zero likelihood for the full joint.
layer2.telemetry: Neural multi-modal coherence across sensory pathways

primitives.name: Mnemonization
primitives.verbatim_quote: Stimuli for the sign only are present, but the stimuli for the significate and the signified means-end-relations are absent.
primitives.assumptions: The sign is recognized independently, while the significate and means-end relations are stored as prior associations.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Memory formation occurs when sign alone triggers retrieval of previously established connections.

layer2.mapping: Represents memory as conditional probability P(significate, means-end | sign), where the sign acts as an index to retrieve stored associations.

primitives.name: Inference
primitives.verbatim_quote: Stimuli for the significate and the signified means-end-relations are absent.
primitives.assumptions: No direct evidence for the target significate and means-end relation exists; only indirect support from related experiences.
primitives.breakdown_regime: Inference emerges when the organism constructs a plausible whole from partial, fragmented cues.

layer2.mapping: Models inference as a generative process P(significate, means-end | observed features), where the organism synthesizes missing components based on learned dependencies.
layer2.telemetry: Prefrontal cortex activation during abductive reasoning tasks

primitives.name: Direction-Distance Correlation
primitives.verbatim_quote: In fact, we shall now assert that what we are here calling sign-gestalts are in fact no more than direction-distance correlations with, however, a further emphasis upon their whole-like or "gestalted" character.
primitives.assumptions: A Gestalt can be represented as a vector of directional relationships and scalar distances between its constituent elements.
primitives.breakdown_regime: The whole emerges from the collective alignment of these directional-scalar pairs; deviation disrupts the Gestalt integrity.

layer2.mapping: Encodes the signgestalt as a covariance matrix capturing pairwise direction-distance statistics, highlighting holistic configuration over individual parts.
layer2.telemetry: Structural similarity in neural population activity patterns
